messages.content: Explain what DNA does in a living cell. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: DNA stores the genetic instructions a cell needs to build and operate itself, encoded in sequences of four chemical bases. When the cell needs to make a protein, specific sections of DNA are transcribed into RNA, which is then translated into chains of amino acids that fold into functional molecules. DNA also copies itself before a cell divides, ensuring that each new cell inherits a complete set of instructions. In this way, it serves as both the cell's working manual and the hereditary material passed from one generation to the next.
